pool.text: A particle of mass 8 kg is moving under the action of a net force \( \mathbf{F} \) N. The acceleration of the particle, \( \mathbf{a} \) m/s\(^2\), is given by the vector \( \mathbf{a} = \begin{pmatrix} 2t - 4 \\ t^2 - 9 \end{pmatrix} \) for \( t \ge 0 \), where \( t \) is the time in seconds. Find the magnitude of the net force acting on the particle at \( t = 3 \) seconds.
pool.sol:
At \( t = 3 \) seconds, the acceleration vector is:
\[ \mathbf{a}(3) = \begin{pmatrix} 2(3) - 4 \\ 3^2 - 9 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}\text{ m/s}^2. \]
By Newton's Second Law, \( \mathbf{F}(3) = m\mathbf{a}(3) = 8\begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 16 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}\text{ N} \), so the magnitude of the net force is \( |\mathbf{F}(3)| = 16\text{ N} \). [M1][A1]

pool.text:
A particle of mass \(2 \text{ kg}\) is acted upon by a constant force \(\mathbf{F}\). At time \(t=0\), the particle is at the origin \((0,0)\) and has velocity \(\mathbf{v} = (3\mathbf{i} + 4\mathbf{j}) \text{ m/s}\). At time \(t=2 \text{ s}\), the particle's velocity is \(\mathbf{v} = (7\mathbf{i} + 12\mathbf{j}) \text{ m/s}\).

Determine the magnitude of the constant force \(\mathbf{F}\) acting on the particle.
pool.sol:
We are given the mass of the particle \(m = 2 \text{ kg}\).
The initial velocity at \(t=0\) is \(\mathbf{v}_0 = (2\mathbf{i} + 8\mathbf{j}) \text{ m/s}\).
The final velocity at \(t=2 \text{ s}\) is \(\mathbf{v}_f = (7\mathbf{i} + 28\mathbf{j}) \text{ m/s}\).

The change in velocity is \(\Delta \mathbf{v} = \mathbf{v}_f - \mathbf{v}_0\).
\(\Delta \mathbf{v} = (7\mathbf{i} + 28\mathbf{j}) - (2\mathbf{i} + 8\mathbf{j}) = (7-2)\mathbf{i} + (28-8)\mathbf{j} = 5\mathbf{i} + 20\mathbf{j} \text{ m/s}\).

The time interval is \(\Delta t = 2 \text{ s}\).

Since the force is constant, the acceleration \(\mathbf{a}\) is also constant.
We can calculate the acceleration using the formula \(\mathbf{a} = \frac{\Delta \mathbf{v}}{\Delta t}\).
\(\mathbf{a} = \frac{5\mathbf{i} + 20\mathbf{j}}{2} = \left(\frac{5}{2}\right)\mathbf{i} + \left(\frac{20}{2}\right)\mathbf{j} = 2.5\mathbf{i} + 10\mathbf{j} \text{ m/s}^2\).

According to Newton's second law of motion, the force \(\mathbf{F}\) acting on the particle is given by \(\mathbf{F} = m\mathbf{a}\).
\(\mathbf{F} = 2 \times (2.5\mathbf{i} + 10\mathbf{j}) = (2 \times 2.5)\mathbf{i} + (2 \times 10)\mathbf{j} = 5\mathbf{i} + 20\mathbf{j} \text{ N}\).

The magnitude of the force \(\mathbf{F}\) is calculated as \(|\mathbf{F}| = \sqrt{F_x^2 + F_y^2}\).
\(|\mathbf{F}| = \sqrt{5^2 + 20^2} = \sqrt{25 + 400} = \sqrt{425}\).

To simplify \(\sqrt{425}\), we find the prime factorization of 425:
\(425 = 5 \times 85 = 5 \times 5 \times 17 = 5^2 \times 17\).

So, \(\sqrt{425} = \sqrt{5^2 \times 17} = \sqrt{5^2} \times \sqrt{17} = 5\sqrt{17}\).

Therefore, the magnitude of the constant force \(\mathbf{F}\) is \(5\sqrt{17} \text{ N}\).

Comparing this with the given choices:
Choice A: \(\frac{5\sqrt{17}}{2} \text{ N}\)
Choice B: \(5\sqrt{17} \text{ N}\)
Choice C: \(\frac{5\sqrt{2}}{2} \text{ N}\)
Choice D: \(5\sqrt{2} \text{ N}\)

Our calculated magnitude matches Choice B. [M1][A1]
